newsitem.title: USA: Law clears way for DeKalb Cty, Ga., tax referendum.
newsitem.headline: Law clears way for DeKalb Cty, Ga., tax referendum.

text.p: Georgia Gov. Zell Miller has signed a law allowing DeKalb County to use a sales tax increase to offset a rollback in property taxes, Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported Thursday.
The homestead option sales tax law was granted fast-track status in the Legislature and clears the way for a March 18 referendum in the Dekalb County.

If voters approve the referendum, the county's sales tax would rise to six percent from five percent. Homeowners would receive a 100 percent exemption from county property taxes, an annual savings of $793 for the owner of a $150,000 house.

Homeowners would still be subject to ad valorem taxes levied for schools and other capital projects. DeKalb's property tax rate would drop from one of the highest in the Atlanta metropolitan area to the lowest.
The law could also apply in six other counties that either don't have local-option or special-use taxes, or where they are about to expire.
